title: Swap linear dielectric for antiferroelectric charge-burst capacitor dielectric
idea: Replace the ZrO2/Al2O3 linear cap dielectric with a field-induced antiferroelectric (ZrO2-rich HfZrO or Pb-free NaNbO3-based) whose AFE-to-FE transition sits just below the write voltage, so writing a '1' adds the released polarization (~15-25 uC/cm2) to the linear charge. At zero field the film relaxes back to the non-polar phase, so there is no remanent imprint and the cell stays a volatile DRAM cell.
why: Capacitor charge wall (fact 1): 2-3x stored charge per pillar at today's AR ~60:1, or the same 5 fF at AR ~25:1, which also makes 3D tiers easier.

title: Swap ZrO2 for cryogenic quantum-paraelectric SrTiO3 storage dielectric
idea: Operate the array at 20-77 K and use SrTiO3 or KTaO3, whose permittivity climbs toward 10^3-10^4 as quantum fluctuations suppress the ferroelectric transition. A planar or AR<5:1 MIM cap then reaches 5 fF in a 12-nm-class cell footprint, aimed at cryo-cooled AI and quantum-computing racks.
why: Removes the 60-75:1 pillar etch (facts 1, 4). Planar caps cut capacitor process steps by ~50%, and leakage freeze-out also cuts refresh (fact 3). The honest cost is cooling power.

title: Swap single dielectric for negative-capacitance ferroelectric/dielectric series stack
idea: Put a 2-3 nm ferroelectric HZO layer in series with the ZrO2 dielectric, with thicknesses tuned so the ferroelectric's negative-slope region partly cancels the series 1/C term. The stack's capacitance then exceeds the dielectric alone, as transient negative-capacitance experiments showed with 2-3x boosts.
why: Facts 1 and 10 (charge wall, voltage floor): the same charge at ~60% of the voltage, or ~2x Cs in the same pillar.

title: Swap ferromagnet for antiferromagnetic Neel-vector bit with zero stray field
idea: Store the bit in the Neel vector of a non-collinear antiferromagnet (Mn3Sn, Mn3Pt) or of Mn2Au. Neel spin-orbit torque switches it in picoseconds, and it is read through an all-antiferromagnetic tunnel junction (tunnelling magnetoresistance was shown in 2023).
why: Non-volatile, so no refresh (fact 3); immune to field and row-hammer disturbance (fact 9); ps writes. With no dipolar crosstalk, cells pack at litho pitch, which FM MRAM cannot do.

title: Swap stored charge for snap-through state of buckled nanobeam
idea: A compressively prestressed SiN or diamond-like-carbon nanobeam (~15 x 150 nm) clamped over a recess has two mirror-image buckled states. A 1-2 ns electrostatic pulse from a side electrode snaps it over, and the state is read capacitively without disturbing it.
why: No leakage path, so no refresh (fact 3); non-destructive read removes restore energy (fact 8); immune to radiation and row hammer (fact 9).

title: Swap capacitor electrons for flux quantum in kinetic-inductance nanowire loop
idea: At 4 K, a NbN or NbTiN nanowire loop whose kinetic inductance is ~100x its geometric inductance stores one flux quantum in under 1 um2. It is written and read by nanocryotron (nTron) gates instead of large Josephson junctions.
why: Zero static power, ~aJ writes and no refresh for superconducting and quantum processors, which then need no room-temperature DRAM; ~10x denser than SFQ memory built on geometric inductance.

title: Swap 30,000-electron capacitor for 200-electron node plus single-electron sensor
idea: Shrink the storage node to a ~0.03 fF gate island and read it with a room-temperature silicon single-electron transistor shared by a few cells. The transistor's sub-3-nm dot is formed by a dopant cluster or an oxidised nanowire constriction, and its Coulomb oscillation turns a few-electron change into a large current swing.
why: Breaks the charge wall outright (fact 1): the storage element needs no capacitor, so the cell is planar and easy to stack for 3D (fact 2).

title: Swap gate-dielectric polarization for ferroelectric semiconductor channel (alpha-In2Se3)
idea: Use a 2D ferroelectric semiconductor such as alpha-In2Se3, where the polarization lives inside the channel itself. Flipping it shifts the band bending and so the channel conductance, with no ferroelectric/dielectric interface to trap charge or depolarize.
why: Gives a capacitor-less 1T cell with non-destructive read and no refresh (facts 1, 3, 8), and avoids the endurance loss that limits HZO FeFETs.

title: Swap solid dielectric for superionic RbAg4I5 electric-double-layer storage node
idea: Fill the storage node with a room-temperature superionic conductor (RbAg4I5, ~0.3 S/cm) against an ion-blocking electrode. The bit is held as a sub-nm Helmholtz double layer (~10-20 uF/cm2), and the high ionic conductivity keeps the RC charging time near ~10 ns at nanoscale.
why: Fact 1: 2-3x charge per area over an EOT-0.5 nm dielectric, multiplied by porous electrode area, so short pillars with AR ~20:1 can be used.

title: Swap oxide ferroelectric for vapor-deposited molecular ferroelectric croconic acid
idea: Use a proton-tautomerism organic ferroelectric (croconic acid, Pr ~20 uC/cm2, or DIPAB) evaporated onto the cap electrode at <150 C. It switches by proton transfer, not oxygen-vacancy motion, so HZO's vacancy-driven wake-up and fatigue are absent.
why: A low-temperature BEOL storage layer for monolithic stacking above logic, with periphery under the array (fact 7), and no rare inputs; the target is FeRAM-class endurance beyond 10^12 cycles.

title: Swap charge for molecular spin state in spin-crossover nanocrystals
idea: Store the bit as the low-spin or high-spin state of Fe(II)-triazole spin-crossover nanocrystals, which are bistable inside a thermal hysteresis loop centred on the die's operating temperature. A field or current pulse switches the state, and the read senses the ~10^2 change in conductance or permittivity.
why: Non-volatile, so no refresh (fact 3). The solution chemistry is cheap, uses abundant Fe and N with no chokepoint elements, and makes a 2-terminal crossbar that stacks.

title: Swap silicon storage node for 4H-SiC junction-isolated node
idea: Build the 1T1C or gain-cell storage node in 4H-SiC, whose 3.26 eV bandgap cuts junction generation leakage by >10^15 versus Si. SiC DRAM test cells in the 1990s already held data for hours to years at room temperature.
why: Removes refresh (fact 3: ~46 fJ/bit and 10-20% of bandwidth). SiC boules grow without Spruce Pine quartz crucibles, and U.S. SiC fabs (NC, NY) already exist, which helps U.S. manufacturing.

title: Swap voltage level for oscillation phase: nanoscale parametron bit
idea: Revive Goto's parametron at the nanoscale. Each cell is a nanomechanical or LC resonator pumped at 2f by a shared clock, the bit is the 0 or pi phase of its subharmonic oscillation (which the pump keeps locked), and the cell is read by phase comparison with a reference.
why: The bit is a binary phase, not a leaking charge, so there is no refresh (fact 3) and no charge-disturb row hammer (fact 9). Adiabatic quantum-flux-parametron versions at 4 K reach zJ switching.

title: Swap charge for ferroelastic twin variant read by piezoresistance
idea: Store the bit as which of two ferroelastic twin orientations a nanocrystal adopts (for example tetragonal-twin BiFeO3 or a NiTi martensite nanopillar). A strain pulse from an integrated AlN piezo layer switches it, and the read uses the anisotropic piezoresistance of an underlying channel.
why: Non-volatile with non-destructive read (facts 3, 8); voltage-driven at <0.5 V through piezo coupling (fact 10).

title: Swap capacitor for single deep-donor atom charge state
idea: Place one deep donor (Se or Te in Si, ~0.3 eV) per cell by deterministic single-ion implantation or hydrogen-resist STM lithography. Its neutral or ionized charge state is the bit, read by a nearby charge sensor.
why: Ultimate density, about one nm2 per bit (facts 2, 4); the deep level keeps the bit stable at room temperature, which shallow P donors cannot do.

title: Swap tungsten/platinum spin-orbit layer for chiral-molecule spin filter
idea: Write a nanomagnet bit by chiral-induced spin selectivity (CISS): a self-assembled monolayer of helical molecules (helicenes or alpha-helix peptides) spin-polarizes the write current, replacing heavy-metal W/Pt/Ta spin-orbit-torque layers.
why: Takes tungsten (China ~80%) and platinum-group metals out of non-volatile working memory, and the monolayer self-assembles with no lithography (scarce-resource axis).

title: Swap leaky capacitor for series resonant-tunnelling-diode latch (TSRAM)
idea: Two vertically stacked resonant-tunnelling diodes (Si/SiGe, InGaAs/AlAs or graphene/hBN) in series form a bistable latch held at valley current (<10 pA). With one pass transistor for access, it is a static cell about the size of 1T1C.
why: Refresh-free static storage (fact 3) at ~10 mA standby per Gb, no tall capacitor (fact 1) and non-destructive read (fact 8).

title: Swap stored charge for conducting ferroelectric domain wall presence
idea: In thin-film LiNbO3 or BiFeO3 mesa cells, the bit is whether a charged, conducting domain wall bridges two side electrodes. Writing creates or erases the wall in ns, and reading senses wall conduction (on/off >10^4) without switching polarization.
why: Non-destructive read cuts the restore share of the ~5.9 pJ/bit destructive read (fact 8); non-volatile, so no refresh (fact 3); cycling above 10^10 has been reported.

title: Swap ionic ferroelectric for sliding-stacking ferroelectric tunnel barrier
idea: Use parallel-stacked bilayer hBN or 3R-MoS2 as an atomically thin tunnel barrier whose out-of-plane polarization flips when the layers slide by one-third of a unit cell. No ions move and no bonds break, so the cell should be fatigue-free, and the polarization modulates the tunnelling current for non-destructive read.
why: Turns endurance-limited ferroelectric memory into DRAM-endurance memory (>10^15 cycles targeted) at ~0.5 V (fact 10), and non-volatility removes refresh (fact 3).

title: Swap current-driven magnet for voltage-flipped magnetoelectric BiFeO3 bit
idea: Exchange-couple a CoFe nanomagnet to multiferroic BiFeO3. A 100 mV field flips the BiFeO3 polarization and antiferromagnetic order, which drags the magnet with it, and the state is read through inverse Rashba-Edelstein charge output, as in MESO.
why: Breaks the voltage floor (fact 10): a ~100 mV write needs ~10-30x less CV2 energy than a 1-3 V DRAM write, and storage is non-volatile.

title: Swap charge for metastable charge-density-wave hidden state in 1T-TaS2
idea: A ~30 ps electrical pulse of ~fJ switches a nanoscale 1T-TaS2 cell from its insulating commensurate CDW into a metastable metallic hidden state, and a longer pulse resets it. The bit is the electronic order, read as a ~100x resistance ratio.
why: fJ, ps writes for the energy and speed axes. The hidden state is long-lived only below ~100 K, so this suits cryo AI racks or strain-stabilized films.

title: Swap SiO2 tunnel barrier for InAs/AlSb resonant triple barrier
idea: Store charge on an InAs floating gate isolated by an InAs/AlSb triple-barrier resonant-tunnelling structure (ULTRARAM-style). At about 2.5 V the resonance aligns and electrons tunnel quickly at low energy; at 0 V the 2.1 eV AlSb conduction-band offset blocks them, so retention exceeds years.
why: A non-volatile, DRAM-speed cell with endurance above 10^7 already shown, ~100x lower switching energy per area than DRAM, and no refresh (fact 3); it is grown on Si by MBE, a tool set available in the U.S.

title: Swap hafnia for wurtzite AlScN ferroelectric with 5x remanent charge
idea: Use sputtered Al0.7Sc0.3N (Pr ~100-120 uC/cm2, about 5x HZO), deposited at <=400 C, as the switching layer of a 1T1C cell. The larger switched charge lets a planar or AR-10:1 capacitor give a full DRAM-class signal.
why: Charge wall (fact 1): ~5x charge per area removes high-AR pillars, and nitride sputtering is cheap and available in the U.S. Scandium supply and endurance are the risks.

title: Swap EUV hole patterning for guided anodic-alumina self-ordered pores
idea: Deposit 2-3 um of aluminum over DUV-made access transistors and imprint shallow DUV-defined pits at the landing-pad positions. Anodizing then nucleates pores at the pits, which self-order into ~25 nm holes with AR above 100:1, and ALD TiN/ZrO2/TiN lines them as storage capacitors.
why: Exceeds the 60-75:1 pillar AR wall (fact 1) without EUV or a high-AR plasma etch (fact 4). The wet electrochemical step costs a few dollars per wafer and uses tools from the aluminum-capacitor industry.

title: Swap EUV contact holes for block-copolymer cylinder self-assembly
idea: Coat a high-chi block copolymer (PS-b-PDMS or PS-b-P2VP) into relaxed-pitch DUV guide holes, so each guide splits into a cluster of 3-7 cylinders at ~24 nm pitch. The cylinders are then transferred into the hard mask that defines the storage-node holes.
why: Replaces 2-3 of the 5-7 EUV layers (fact 4) with a spin-coat and anneal, cutting ~20-30% of litho-driven wafer cost.

title: Swap tall pillar for on-chip multilayer-ceramic nanolaminate capacitor
idea: Deposit ~100 alternating ALD layers of TiN (3 nm) and ZrO2 (4 nm) and cut each cell block with one DUV etch. Then recess and insulate the odd electrodes on one sidewall and the even ones on the other (like MLCC end terminations), so all plates connect in parallel.
why: ~100 stacked parallel plates give pillar-class Cs (fact 1) from a ~0.7 um low-AR block at DUV pitch, with no EUV and no 60:1 etch (fact 4).

title: Swap layer-by-layer 3D stacking for rolling one patterned membrane
idea: Pattern one planar layer of thin-film gain cells with DUV on a strained SiNx bilayer, release it, and let the built-in strain roll it into a 20-winding tube. Each winding becomes a memory tier, and the tiers connect through edge contacts along the roll axis.
why: Gives 20 tiers from one deposition and patterning sequence (fact 2), so cost does not grow with the tier count, and no EUV is used (fact 4).

title: Swap plasma etching for metal-assisted chemical etching of deep trenches
idea: Pattern a Pt or Ag catalyst mesh by DUV (or by dewetting) and immerse it in HF/H2O2. The catalyst sinks straight into the silicon, cutting vertical holes with AR above 200:1 and no plasma damage, and ALD MIM lines them as IBM-style deep-trench storage capacitors under the access transistor.
why: ~3x the AR of today's pillars gives ~3x Cs (fact 1), or the same Cs at a relaxed DUV diameter, with no EUV and a cheap wet bench instead of high-power etch tools (fact 4).

title: Swap litho-defined cells for thickness-defined annular capacitors in stacks
idea: In a 64-pair Si/SiGe stack, etch one DUV hole per cell column and selectively recess the SiGe laterally into ring cavities whose height is set by film thickness (~8 nm). ALD fills them as ring capacitors, each wired to the lateral transistor in its tier.
why: Solves the 3D capacitor blocker (fact 2): deposition thickness, not lithography, sets the critical dimension, so 64 tiers need one DUV litho step (fact 4).

title: Swap dielectric charge for porphyrin redox monolayer storing discrete electrons
idea: Graft a tripodal porphyrin or ferrocene self-assembled monolayer onto the storage electrode, with a solid electrolyte. The bit is held as molecular oxidation states (two states give 1.5 bits per cell) at ~10^14 molecules/cm2, or about 16-30 uC/cm2 per state; ZettaCore showed 400 C survivability and 10^12 cycles.
why: 3-4x charge per area over a linear cap (fact 1), so a 15:1 cap at DUV pitch works, and retention of minutes cuts refresh ~1000x (fact 3); the monolayer self-assembles with no lithography.

title: Swap inert TiN electrode for pseudocapacitive MXene intercalation electrode
idea: Coat the storage node with a Ti3C2 MXene film against a thin solid proton conductor. Proton intercalation between MXene layers adds Faradaic pseudocapacitance (hundreds of uF/cm2 in bulk) to the double layer, and MXenes are among the fastest-rate pseudocapacitive materials known.
why: Over 10x areal capacitance (fact 1) from abundant Ti and C, unlike RuO2, which needs scarce Ru; a planar or shallow cap at DUV pitch can store DRAM-level charge.

title: Swap ZrO2 for high-entropy relaxor perovskite with k near 500
idea: Deposit a lead-free high-entropy relaxor such as (Ba,Sr)(Ti,Zr,Hf,Sn)O3, whose polar nanoregions give a slim, nearly linear loop and k ~300-800 in 15-20 nm films. Crystallize it by flash-lamp anneal to keep the CMOS below within its thermal budget.
why: ~10x k gives 5 fF from a 10:1 cap at 30-40 nm DUV pitch (facts 1, 4); entropy stabilization targets the leakage and thickness-scaling failures that ended 2000-era BST.

title: Swap per-bit access transistors for vertical CCD charge-packet strings
idea: Reuse the 3D NAND stack: each vertical poly or IGZO channel works as a CCD in which the 128 tier gates, clocked in three phases, shift ~40 charge packets up and down to a regenerating sense amplifier at the top. There is no contact, capacitor or access transistor per bit, and each pass through the amplifier refreshes the packet.
why: ~1 bit per 250 nm2 (better than 864 nm2 for 6F2) using only DUV 3D NAND tools (facts 2, 4, 7); no tunnelling, so endurance is unlimited; average shift latency is ~20 ns.

title: Swap capacitor for vertical gated thyristor bistable latch
idea: A vertical p-n-p-n silicon thyristor with a gated base holds the bit regeneratively: latched on or blocked off, with gate pulses giving ns switching (the T-RAM/VLT lineage). It is built at 4F2 with F = 28-40 nm using DUV double patterning.
why: Static, capacitor-less storage (fact 1) with no refresh (fact 3). Because the device is vertical it can be stacked, and two tiers roughly match the bit density of EUV 6F2 at F = 12 nm without EUV (fact 4).

title: Swap binary charge for eight-level charge with shared SAR sensing
idea: At relaxed DUV pitch (F ~ 20 nm) the larger cell cap stores eight charge levels (3 bits). They are read by a charge-redistribution SAR sense amplifier shared across four bitlines, protected by a strong symbol ECC, and refreshed at a rate set by the narrowest level margin.
why: 3 bits per cell offsets the ~2.8x area loss of skipping EUV (fact 4), giving equal or better bits per mm2 with no EUV capex.

title: Swap room temperature for 77 K to freeze leakage, planar caps
idea: Run 1T1C cells made on a 28-nm DUV logic process in liquid-nitrogen-immersed memory sleds. At 77 K, junction and GIDL leakage fall by >10^6 and Cu wiring resistance falls ~5x, so a ~1 fF planar MIM cap keeps data for hours and is sensed on short, low-capacitance bitlines.
why: Turns any mature DUV logic fab into a DRAM source with no pillar etch and no EUV (facts 1, 4), and refresh all but disappears (fact 3). LN2 cooling costs ~10 W per watt removed.

title: Swap lithography for thermal fiber drawing of capacitor preforms
idea: Build a cm-scale preform of coaxial metal/glass capacitors and thermally draw it 10^4x into fibers with sub-50-nm features. Stack and redraw the fibers into an ordered bundle (as in fiber-optic faceplates), then slice it into capacitor wafers bonded onto DUV access-transistor arrays with oversized landing pads.
why: Makes nanoscale storage capacitors with no lithography at all (fact 4), at drawing rates of km per hour, using furnaces instead of fabs (capital axis).

title: Swap big capacitor for small charge plus electron-multiplying readout
idea: Store only ~500 electrons on a shallow capacitor at DUV pitch. At read, the packet passes through a short EMCCD-style impact-ionization gain register on the bitline (gain ~20-100) before the sense amplifier.
why: Needs ~10x less Cs (fact 1), so planar or AR <8:1 caps work without EUV or a high-AR etch (fact 4); EMCCD gain registers already reach sub-electron noise.

title: Swap destructive charge dump for small-signal capacitive ferroelectric read
idea: Build asymmetric-electrode ferroelectric capacitors (for example TiN/HZO/W-oxide) whose small-signal capacitance differs by 20-40% between the two polarization states. A ~100 mV AC probe senses that capacitance without switching the cell, and the films stack in 3D by deposition at DUV pitch.
why: No destructive read and no write-back (fact 8), and no refresh (fact 3). Writes are rare, so ferroelectric endurance limits matter less, and 3D stacking by deposition needs no EUV (facts 2, 4).

title: Swap 3D NAND thick tunnel oxide for direct-tunnel volatile trap
idea: Run existing DUV 3D NAND lines with a ~1.5-2 nm direct-tunnelling oxide under the nitride trap. The cells write in ~10-50 ns at <4 V, keep data for seconds to minutes (refreshed like DRAM) and avoid Fowler-Nordheim damage, aiming at >10^14 cycles.
why: Puts 200+-layer 3D NAND capacity, which needs no EUV, to work as volatile working memory at DRAM-class density or better (facts 2, 4). The fabs and tools already exist, including in the U.S.

title: Swap fixed capacitor for gated-diode varactor that amplifies on read
idea: Store charge in the inversion layer of a gated diode (IBM 2T1D cell). At read the gate is pulsed: a stored '1' keeps its inversion capacitance and boosts the node voltage several-fold, while a '0' collapses to depletion capacitance, which gives built-in voltage gain.
why: The signal gain lets ~1 fF planar storage work (fact 1) with only mature-node DUV (fact 4), and lowers bitline-swing energy (fact 10).

title: Swap smooth electrode for dealloyed nanoporous metal sponge electrode
idea: Deposit an AlTi or AgAu alloy as the storage-node electrode and selectively dissolve the less noble element, leaving a nanoporous sponge with 5-10 nm ligaments and 10-30x the surface area. ALD then coats the dielectric and top electrode conformally.
why: 10x or more effective area per footprint breaks the charge wall (fact 1) with a short, relaxed-pitch DUV cap and no high-AR etch or EUV (fact 4).

title: Swap electron storage for proton position in hydrated-oxide gate
idea: A 3-terminal cell shuttles H+ between a Pd-H reservoir and a WO3 channel through a 5 nm phosphosilicate-glass proton conductor. Pulses of ~5 ns at ~1 V (as in MIT's protonic resistors) set the channel conductance, which is read non-destructively.
why: Retention of hours to days cuts refresh (fact 3) and non-destructive read helps fact 8. The films are deposition-defined at DUV pitch, and protons need no scarce elements.

title: Swap EUV masks for maskless two-beam interference lattice exposure
idea: Memory arrays are periodic, so expose the capacitor and wordline lattices by 193-nm immersion two-beam interference (~40 nm pitch per pass). Double exposure with the grating rotated forms the hole lattice, and a cheap DUV trim mask cuts the array edges.
why: Replaces EUV for the dense periodic layers (fact 4) with a simpler, cheaper interference tool that needs no mask set and could be built in the U.S.

title: Swap litho-patterned storage nodes for area-selective bottom-up growth
idea: Use area-selective ALD/CVD (inhibitor self-assembled monolayers on the dielectric, so growth occurs only on metal landing pads) to grow TiN storage-node pillars upward from each contact. The node layer copies the DUV-made contact pattern with no lithography or etch of its own.
why: Removes one or two critical litho/etch layers (fact 4) and the high-AR etch (fact 1); the pillars are self-aligned, so there is no overlay error.

title: Swap one-physics capacitor for dual polarization-plus-charge two-bit cell
idea: Use a ferroelectric-dielectric capacitor that stores two independent bits: the polarization direction (non-volatile) and the linear charge magnitude (volatile). The read has two phases: a sub-coercive pulse senses the linear charge first, then a switching pulse with write-back senses the polarization.
why: 2 bits per DUV cell offsets the pitch loss from skipping EUV (fact 4), and the polarization bit survives power loss, so it can hold checkpoints.
